conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I’m Dr. Lee. You’re here today for a planned surgery to create a new dialysis access in your left arm, correct?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s right. I’ve been on dialysis through the catheter in my neck, but they said it’s better to have a graft in my arm.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We’re going to place a loop graft in your left arm so you can have more reliable and safer long-term dialysis access.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I heard they might use a synthetic tube. Is that normal?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we used a PTFE graft because your vessels have some calcification. It’s a strong, safe material that works well for patients like you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I’m a little worried about my hand going numb or cold after this. I’ve had circulation issues before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a valid concern. We checked during surgery, and there’s a good pulse in your wrist. Your hand is a bit cooler than the other side, but that’s expected and close to your baseline.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the numbness in my fingertips? That’s been there a while, but I don’t want it to get worse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You mentioned mild numbness, which we believe is related to your diabetic neuropathy. We didn’t see any new nerve issues from the surgery.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just checking in. How’s your left arm feeling? Any pain, coldness, or blue fingers?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No pain, no blue fingers. It’s still a little cool, and the tips of my fingers are numb like usual.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We’re watching closely for any signs of poor blood flow. The graft has a strong thrill and bruit, which means it’s working well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You just finished your dialysis session through the neck catheter. Everything went smoothly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. So now what? Is the new graft ready to use?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not yet. It needs about 2–3 weeks to mature before we can use it for dialysis. You’ll keep using your neck catheter until then.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re planning to discharge you today. Your graft is patent, and your hand exam remains stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What should I watch for at home? I don’t want to miss anything serious.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call the access clinic immediately if you have fevers, pain, coldness, or blue fingers in the left hand. Also check daily for the thrill—the buzzing feeling over the graft.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And if I don’t feel the buzz?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That could mean the graft is blocked. Call right away—don’t wait for your next dialysis. Also, no blood pressures or needle sticks in that arm.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. No heavy lifting either, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Keep it under 10 pounds, and avoid tight clothes or jewelry on that side. Elevate your arm to reduce swelling.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your discharge orders are ready. You’ll continue all your regular medications, including insulin and apixaban.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the pain medicine?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You have tramadol for mild pain and now also hydrocodone for breakthrough pain—take only as needed. And we added docusate for constipation prevention.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I feel ready to go home now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. Keep your follow-up with the access team, and continue dialysis as scheduled.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All set. You’re cleared to go home with services. Take care, and call if anything changes with your arm.
